walkthroughs.body_html:
Formation of Planetary Systems — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Formation of Planetary Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Formation of Planetary Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Earth is closer to the Sun in summer.
Earth's axial tilt - 23.5 degrees - causes different hemispheres to receive more direct sunlight at different times of year.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It moves backwards.
It is the hottest stage.

mcqs.q: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
options: It moves backwards.
It does not clear its orbital neighbourhood of similar-sized bodies.
It is too small to be a planet.
The Sun's intensity changes throughout the year.
